children: With markets pricing more than 25 basis points of Fed tightening by the year-end, the yen hitting 160 against the dollar again wouldn't be surprising, says Masahiko Loo at State Street Investment Management. The yen weakening toward 160 inevitably revives intervention talk, but markets may be underestimating Tokyo's toolkit, the chief fixed-income strategist writes. "Much of the focus remains on spot intervention, yet facilities such as the Fed's FIMA repo facility provide additional flexibility in mobilizing dollar liquidity without forcing outright sales of longer-duration U.S. assets." The mid-160s may be just another level to the market, but that range could attract a much stronger policy response than investors currently anticipate, Loo says. The dollar is last at 159.81 yen, LSEG data shows. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)
